_comment: forest_canopy: Map 3's wood as map geometry, one chunk at identity. Every tree row of forest_trees.LAYOUT (113: 45 a, 30 b, 38 c) sculpted at its own place and scale against the real lane roof (forest_build's ground, whose underside now dips over the trees and lifts over open lane): the prop's trunk (its first eight rings, the cover footprint) carried on to a fork half way to the roof, two or three heavy boughs sweeping out then up, one secondary off each, the trunk's top as a thick leader, and the foliage as irregular stretched leaf masses (a wobbly rim, a skewed mid ring, a keel) -- one round every bough tip, one round the leader's head, one crown mass over the trunk whose rim lies ON the roof's own triangulated underside (buried 0.10 m); any mass whose top comes within 0.9 m of the roof merges its rim into it too. Masses of neighbouring trees overlap into one shared canopy; undersides are shade, flanks leaf. One material (the forest atlas, external PNG), one mesh of closed shells (one per tree, one per leaf mass). ForestCanopyCollision is the purpose-built collider shipped as a `-colonly` node: every tree's own prop collider (forest_tree_prop_build.build_collider, the trunk's silhouette to ring 6) at that tree's transform, so the bake and the cover finder see the same triangles the 113 prop instances gave them. Godot turns it into a StaticBody3D + ConcavePolygonShape3D and drops its mesh, so `surfaces` counts only what is drawn.
